segments.narration: Fourteen men walked into the Florida sky and never returned. On December 5, 1945, five TBM Avenger torpedo bombers lifted off from Fort Lauderdale for a routine training mission.
Hours later, radio operators caught a chilling distress call. The flight leader reported that both of his compasses had failed, and nothing looked familiar below them.
As the squadron flew in widening circles over the open ocean, darkness set in. But the mystery deepened when a rescue seaplane sent to find them vanished in a fiery explosion.
Investigators piecing together the tragedy discovered the likely answer. Disoriented by navigational errors and severe weather, the squadron simply ran out of fuel and ditched at sea.
Shifting Atlantic currents and deep trenches ensured the planes vanished forever, leaving behind only an enduring aviation legend.

verdicts.claim: A rescue seaplane sent to find the squadron also exploded mid-air, adding another layer of tragedy.
verdicts.note: A Martin PBM Mariner flying boat sent to search for Flight 19 was lost in an apparent mid-air explosion.

verdicts.claim: Navigational errors, sudden bad weather, and fuel exhaustion caused the squadron to crash into the ocean.
verdicts.note: Investigators concluded that navigation errors led the planes far out to sea, where bad weather and fuel exhaustion forced them to ditch.

verdicts.claim: Shifting Atlantic currents and deep ocean trenches prevented search crews from ever recovering the wreckage.
verdicts.note: The reference mentions that the Navy had neither bodies nor airplanes, but does not state that shifting currents and deep trenches were the specific reasons the wreckage was never recovered.
